Bexley.schoolNote: Townley Grammar and Bexley Grammar are selective. Several good primaries across the borough.
Bexley.floodNote: Thames-side areas (Erith, Thamesmead) have significant flood risk. Inland areas are safe.
Bexley.aqNote: Good air quality across most of the borough. Lower traffic density than inner boroughs.
Bexley.transportNote: Elizabeth Line at Abbey Wood. National Rail to London Bridge. Limited tube access. Some areas car-dependent.
Bexley.healthcareNote: Queen Elizabeth Hospital (Woolwich) nearby. Darent Valley Hospital. Good GP coverage.

Harrow.schoolNote: Harrow School (private, historic). Nower Hill High School is popular. Several Outstanding primaries.
Harrow.floodNote: Low flood risk throughout. Mostly elevated terrain.
Harrow.aqNote: Good air quality in residential areas. Main roads through Harrow town centre are worse.
Harrow.transportNote: Metropolitan Line (fast to Baker Street). Bakerloo to Harrow & Wealdstone. Good bus network.
Harrow.healthcareNote: Northwick Park Hospital (A&E). Good GP coverage. Several health centres.

Queens.schoolNote: Townsend Harris High School is one of NYC best. Good school diversity. Queens has strong public school options.
Queens.floodNote: Severe flood risk in southern coastal areas (Rockaway, Howard Beach). Hurricane Sandy caused major damage.
Queens.aqNote: Airport operations and highway traffic affect air quality. Residential areas away from highways are better.
Queens.transportNote: 7 train, E/F/M/R, LIRR, JFK AirTrain. Flushing is a major hub.
Queens.healthcareNote: Queens Hospital Center, Long Island Jewish Medical Center, NYC Health+Hospitals.
Queens.roadNoiseVintage: Curated borough rating (NYC DOT; not DEFRA, which is England only)

Brooklyn.schoolNote: Brooklyn Tech is a top specialized high school. Strong charter school options. PS/IS networks improving.
Brooklyn.floodNote: Coastal areas (Red Hook, Coney Island, Brighton Beach) have significant flood risk. Interior areas are generally safe.
Brooklyn.aqNote: BQE corridor is a pollution hotspot. Prospect Park area has better air quality.
Brooklyn.transportNote: Multiple subway lines (2/3/4/5/B/D/F/G/N/Q/R), LIRR Atlantic Terminal. Among the best-connected.
Brooklyn.healthcareNote: Brooklyn Methodist, Maimonides, NYU Langone Brooklyn, Kings County Hospital.
Brooklyn.roadNoiseVintage: Curated borough rating (NYC DOT; not DEFRA, which is England only)

Manhattan.schoolNote: Stuyvesant, Bronx Science (technically Bronx), multiple elite schools. Best private school density in the US.
Manhattan.floodNote: Lower Manhattan and East Side have significant flood risk. FDR Drive area and Battery Park exposed.
Manhattan.aqNote: High traffic density causes poor air quality. Central Park and riverside areas are better.
Manhattan.transportNote: Every subway line serves Manhattan. PATH to NJ. Metro-North at Grand Central. Unrivalled connectivity.
Manhattan.healthcareNote: NYU Langone, Mount Sinai, NewYork-Presbyterian, Memorial Sloan Kettering. World-class healthcare.
Manhattan.roadNoiseVintage: Curated borough rating (NYC DOT; not DEFRA, which is England only)

Bronx.schoolNote: Bronx Science is a top specialized school. Multiple charter school options. School quality varies significantly by neighbourhood.
Bronx.floodNote: Generally low flood risk except along waterfront areas. Hunts Point has some risk.
Bronx.aqNote: Cross Bronx Expressway is one of the most polluted corridors in NYC. Northern areas have better air.
Bronx.transportNote: 4/5/6, B/D, Metro-North. South Bronx well-connected. Northern areas more car-dependent.
Bronx.healthcareNote: Montefiore Medical Center (major), Lincoln Hospital, Jacobi Medical Center.
Bronx.roadNoiseVintage: Curated borough rating (NYC DOT; not DEFRA, which is England only)

Staten Island.schoolNote: Good suburban-style schools. Staten Island Tech is a specialized high school. Lower class sizes than other boroughs.
Staten Island.floodNote: Eastern and southern shores have severe flood risk. Hurricane Sandy devastated many areas.
Staten Island.aqNote: Best air quality of any NYC borough. Lower traffic density. More green space.
Staten Island.transportNote: Staten Island Railway, free ferry to Manhattan. Very car-dependent. No subway connection.
Staten Island.healthcareNote: Staten Island University Hospital. Limited compared to other boroughs.
Staten Island.roadNoiseVintage: Curated borough rating (NYC DOT; not DEFRA, which is England only)
